Detailed Description

Class representing a call to a PSyclone Kernel with a user-provided
implementation. The kernel may or may not be in-lined.

:param type KernelArguments: the API-specific sub-class of \
                             :py:class:`psyclone.psyGen.Arguments` to \
                             create.
:param call: Details of the call to this kernel in the Algorithm layer.
:type call: :py:class:`psyclone.parse.algorithm.KernelCall`.
:param parent: the parent of this Node (kernel call) in the Schedule.
:type parent: sub-class of :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`.
:param bool check: whether to check for consistency between the \
    kernel metadata and the algorithm layer. Defaults to True.

1713 def _rename_psyir(self, suffix):
1714 '''Rename the PSyIR module and kernel names by adding the supplied
1715 suffix to the names. This change affects the KernCall and
1716 KernelSchedule nodes as well as the kernel metadata declaration.
1717
1718 :param str suffix: the string to insert into the quantity names.
1719
1720 '''
1721 # We need to get the kernel schedule before modifying self.name
1722 kern_schedule = self.get_kernel_schedule()
1723 container = kern_schedule.ancestor(Container)
1724
1725 # Use the suffix to create a new kernel name. This will
1726 # conform to the PSyclone convention of ending in "_code"
1727 orig_mod_name = self.module_name[:]
1728 orig_kern_name = self.name[:]
1729
1730 new_kern_name = self._new_name(orig_kern_name, suffix, "_code")
1731 new_mod_name = self._new_name(orig_mod_name, suffix, "_mod")
1732
1733 # Change the name of this kernel and the associated
1734 # module. These names are used when generating the PSy-layer.
1735 self.name = new_kern_name[:]
1736 self._module_name = new_mod_name[:]
1737 kern_schedule.name = new_kern_name[:]
1738 container.name = new_mod_name[:]
1739
1740 # Change the name of the Kernel Schedule
1741 kern_schedule.name = new_kern_name
1742
1743 # Ensure the metadata points to the correct procedure now. Since this
1744 # routine is general purpose, we won't always have a domain-specific
1745 # Container here and if we don't, it won't have a 'metadata' property.
1746 if hasattr(container, "metadata"):
1747 container.metadata.procedure_name = new_kern_name[:]
1748 # TODO #928 - until the LFRic KernelInterface is fully functional, we
1749 # can't raise language-level PSyIR to LFRic and therefore we have to
1750 # manually fix the name of the procedure within the text that stores
1751 # the kernel metadata.
1752 container_table = container.symbol_table
1753 for sym in container_table.datatypesymbols:
1754 if isinstance(sym.datatype, UnsupportedFortranType):
1755 new_declaration = sym.datatype.declaration.replace(
1756 orig_kern_name, new_kern_name)
1757 # pylint: disable=protected-access
1758 sym._datatype = UnsupportedFortranType(
1759 new_declaration,
1760 partial_datatype=sym.datatype.partial_datatype)
1761 # pylint: enable=protected-access
1762

1562 def ast(self):
1563 '''
1564 Generate and return the fparser2 AST of the kernel source.
1565
1566 :returns: fparser2 AST of the Fortran file containing this kernel.
1567 :rtype: :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Program`
1568 '''
1569 from fparser.common.readfortran import FortranStringReader
1570 from fparser.two import parser
1571 # If we've already got the AST then just return it
1572 if self._fp2_ast:
1573 return self._fp2_ast
1574 # Use the fparser1 AST to generate Fortran source
1575 fortran = self._module_code.tofortran()
1576 # Create an fparser2 Fortran parser
1577 std = Config.get().fortran_standard
1578 my_parser = parser.ParserFactory().create(std=std)
1579 # Parse that Fortran using our parser
1580 reader = FortranStringReader(fortran)
1581 self._fp2_ast = my_parser(reader)
1582 return self._fp2_ast
1583

1493 def lower_to_language_level(self):
1494 '''
1495 In-place replacement of CodedKern concept into language level
1496 PSyIR constructs. The CodedKern is implemented as a Call to a
1497 routine with the appropriate arguments.
1498
1499 :returns: the lowered version of this node.
1500 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.node.Node`
1501
1502 '''
1503 symtab = self.ancestor(InvokeSchedule).symbol_table
1504
1505 if not self.module_inline:
1506 # If it is not module inlined then make sure we generate the kernel
1507 # file (and rename it when necessary).
1508 self.rename_and_write()
1509 # Then find or create the imported RoutineSymbol
1510 try:
1511 # Limit scope to this Invoke, since a kernel with the same name
1512 # may have been inlined from another invoke in the same file,
1513 # but we have it here marked as "not module-inlined"
1514 rsymbol = symtab.lookup(self._name, scope_limit=symtab.node)
1515 except KeyError:
1516 csymbol = symtab.find_or_create(
1517 self._module_name,
1518 symbol_type=ContainerSymbol)
1519 rsymbol = symtab.new_symbol(
1520 self._name,
1521 symbol_type=RoutineSymbol,
1522 # And allow shadowing in case it is also inlined with
1523 # the same name by another invoke
1524 shadowing=True,
1525 interface=ImportInterface(csymbol))
1526 else:
1527 # If its inlined, the symbol must exist
1528 try:
1529 rsymbol = self.scope.symbol_table.lookup(self._name)
1530 except KeyError as err:
1531 raise GenerationError(
1532 f"Cannot generate this kernel call to '{self.name}' "
1533 f"because it is marked as module-inlined but no such "
1534 f"subroutine exists in this module.") from err
1535
1536 # Create Call to the rsymbol with the argument expressions as children
1537 # of the new node
1538 call_node = Call.create(rsymbol, self.arguments.psyir_expressions())
1539
1540 # Swap itself with the appropriate Call node
1541 self.replace_with(call_node)
1542 return call_node

1455 def module_inline(self, value):
1456 '''
1457 Setter for whether or not to module-inline this kernel.
1458
1459 :param bool value: whether or not to module-inline this kernel.
1460 '''
1461 if value is not True:
1462 raise TypeError(
1463 f"The module inline parameter only accepts the type boolean "
1464 f"'True' since module-inlining is irreversible. But found:"
1465 f" '{value}'.")
1466 # Do the same to all kernels in this invoke with the same name.
1467 # This is needed because gen_code/lowering would otherwise add
1468 # an import with the same name and shadow the module-inline routine
1469 # symbol.
1470 # TODO 1823: The transformation could have more control about this by
1471 # giving an option to specify if the module-inline applies to a
1472 # single kernel, the whole invoke or the whole algorithm.
1473 my_schedule = self.ancestor(InvokeSchedule)
1474 for kernel in my_schedule.walk(Kern):
1475 if kernel is self:

Writes the (transformed) AST of this kernel to file and resets the
'modified' flag to False. By default (config.kernel_naming ==
"multiple"), the kernel is re-named so as to be unique within

then no re-naming and output is performed if there is already

to file. If this is not the case then we raise a GenerationError.)

1601 def rename_and_write(self):
1602 '''
1603 Writes the (transformed) AST of this kernel to file and resets the
1604 'modified' flag to False. By default (config.kernel_naming ==
1605 "multiple"), the kernel is re-named so as to be unique within
1606 the kernel output directory stored within the configuration
1607 object. Alternatively, if config.kernel_naming is "single"
1608 then no re-naming and output is performed if there is already
1609 a transformed copy of the kernel in the output dir. (In this
1610 case a check is performed that the transformed kernel already
1611 present is identical to the one that we would otherwise write
1612 to file. If this is not the case then we raise a GenerationError.)
1613
1614 :raises GenerationError: if config.kernel_naming == "single" and a \
1615 different, transformed version of this \
1616 kernel is already in the output directory.
1617 :raises NotImplementedError: if the kernel has been transformed but \
1618 is also flagged for module-inlining.
1619
1620 '''
1621 from psyclone.line_length import FortLineLength
1622
1623 config = Config.get()
1624
1625 # If this kernel has not been transformed we do nothing, also if the
1626 # kernel has been module-inlined, the routine already exist in the
1627 # PSyIR and we don't need to generate a new file with it.
1628 if not self.modified or self.module_inline:
1629 return
1630
1631 # Remove any "_mod" if the file follows the PSyclone naming convention
1632 orig_mod_name = self.module_name[:]
1633 if orig_mod_name.lower().endswith("_mod"):
1634 old_base_name = orig_mod_name[:-4]
1635 else:
1636 old_base_name = orig_mod_name[:]
1637
1638 # We could create a hash of a string built from the name of the
1639 # Algorithm (module), the name/position of the Invoke and the
1640 # index of this kernel within that Invoke. However, that creates
1641 # a very long name so we simply ensure that kernel names are unique
1642 # within the user-supplied kernel-output directory.
1643 name_idx = -1
1644 fdesc = None
1645 while not fdesc:
1646 name_idx += 1
1647 new_suffix = ""
1648
1649 new_suffix += f"_{name_idx}"
1650 new_name = old_base_name + new_suffix + "_mod.f90"
1651
1652 try:
1653 # Atomically attempt to open the new kernel file (in case
1654 # this is part of a parallel build)
1655 fdesc = os.open(
1656 os.path.join(config.kernel_output_dir, new_name),
1657 os.O_CREAT | os.O_WRONLY | os.O_EXCL)
1658 except (OSError, IOError):
1659 # The os.O_CREATE and os.O_EXCL flags in combination mean
1660 # that open() raises an error if the file exists
1661 if config.kernel_naming == "single":
1662 # If the kernel-renaming scheme is such that we only ever
1663 # create one copy of a transformed kernel then we're done
1664 break
1665 continue
1666
1667 # Use the suffix we have determined to rename all relevant quantities
1668 # within the AST of the kernel code.
1669 self._rename_psyir(new_suffix)
1670
1671 # Kernel is now self-consistent so unset the modified flag
1672 self.modified = False
1673
1674 # If we reach this point the kernel needs to be written out into a
1675 # file using a PSyIR back-end. At the moment there is no way to choose
1676 # which back-end to use, so simply use the Fortran one (and limit the
1677 # line length).
1678 fortran_writer = FortranWriter(
1679 check_global_constraints=config.backend_checks_enabled)
1680 # Start from the root of the schedule as we want to output
1681 # any module information surrounding the kernel subroutine
1682 # as well as the subroutine itself.
1683 new_kern_code = fortran_writer(self.get_kernel_schedule().root)
1684 fll = FortLineLength()
1685 new_kern_code = fll.process(new_kern_code)
1686
1687 if not fdesc:
1688 # If we've not got a file descriptor at this point then that's
1689 # because the file already exists and the kernel-naming scheme
1690 # ("single") means we're not creating a new one.
1691 # Check that what we've got is the same as what's in the file
1692 with open(os.path.join(config.kernel_output_dir,
1693 new_name), "r") as ffile:
1694 kern_code = ffile.read()
1695 if kern_code != new_kern_code:
1696 raise GenerationError(
1697 f"A transformed version of this Kernel "
1698 f"'{self._module_name + '''.f90'''}' already exists "
1699 f"in the kernel-output directory "
1700 f"({config.kernel_output_dir}) but is not the "
1701 f"same as the current, transformed kernel and the "
1702 f"kernel-renaming scheme is set to "
1703 f"'{config.kernel_naming}'. (If you wish to"
1704 f" generate a new, unique kernel for every kernel "
1705 f"that is transformed then use "
1706 f"'--kernel-renaming multiple'.)")
1707 else:
1708 # Write the modified AST out to file
1709 os.write(fdesc, new_kern_code.encode())
1710 # Close the new kernel file
1711 os.close(fdesc)

1403 valid_opencl_kernel_options = ['local_size', 'queue_number']
